mainTopic: Vows that do not take effect: why 'חולין' is listed, the source that a נדר needs a דבר הנדור, and when an empty vow still needs a חכם
overview: The גמרא finishes asking whose view the משנה's case of 'חולין' follows. Under רבי מאיר the needed inference does not work, and under רבי יהודה the case repeats the earlier part of the משנה. The first answer is that 'חולין' was simply listed together with pig meat and עבודה זרה. רבינא suggests instead that it teaches that these vows need no שאלה to a חכם. That idea is rejected, because the סיפא already shows this, so 'חולין' was mentioned only in passing. Next the גמרא brings the פסוק 'איש כי ידר נדר לה׳' as the source that a נדר works only when it is linked to a דבר הנדור. It explains that 'לאסור אסר' does not include things the תורה forbids. Then a ברייתא saying 'like my mother's flesh' means nothing seems to contradict the משנה. אביי answers that the vow has no force מדאורייתא but needs שאלה מדרבנן. רבא answers that the ברייתא is about תלמידי חכמים and the משנה is about an עם הארץ. Support for רבא comes from a ברייתא about vowing by the תורה, with the comments of רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן.

steps.title: Finishing the challenge against רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a challenge: if the משנה follows רבי מאיר, how can we infer anything, when he does not derive a 'yes' from a 'no'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really hear a 'yes' from a 'no'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that began just before this point. It argues that the משנה's case of 'חולין' cannot follow רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that you may not take a negative statement and infer its positive opposite. So working out the vow's meaning by flipping it ('not חולין' means 'קרבן') does not fit his view. That makes it hard to attribute this part of the משנה to him.

keyTerms.meaning: From a 'no' you can hear a 'yes': inferring the positive from a negative statement

phrases.english: from a 'no' do you hear a 'yes'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question from the previous section of the daf about whose view the 'חולין' case follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the 'חולין' case follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר does not infer a positive from a negative, so the reasoning the case needs does not fit his view.

steps.title: If it follows רבי יהודה, the case is a repeat
steps.stepSummary: Saying the case follows רבי יהודה does not work either, because the earlier part of the משנה already taught the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is רבי יהודה, this is the same as the first part of the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other option, רבי יהודה. It finds a new problem: the ruling would just repeat something the משנה already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does infer a 'yes' from a 'no'. Under his view, the lesson this case gives by implication is that 'not חולין' ('לחולין') is a binding vow. But the earlier part of the משנה (on daf 10b) already taught exactly that, so this case adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as the first clause
The first or earlier part of a משנה

phrases.english: But rather, if it is רבי יהודה,
that is the same as the first clause!
phrases.notes: The first clause is the earlier משנה on 10b, which already taught that saying 'לחולין' makes a vow take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out רבי מאיר, it tests רבי יהודה and finds the case redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the 'חולין' case follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יהודה the ruling is already known from the רישא, so including it again is unnecessary.

steps.title: 'חולין' was listed only to go along with the others
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה. 'חולין' was included only because the משנה was listing pig meat and עבודה זרה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches 'like pig meat' and 'like עבודה זרה', it therefore also teaches 'חולין'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רבי יהודה. It admits the case is a repeat, but explains why the משנה included it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer accepts that 'חולין' teaches nothing new. Since the משנה was already listing vows that don't take effect, like pig meat and עבודה זרה, it tossed 'חולין' into the same list.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it teaches: something is included only because of the cases around it
Pig meat: something forbidden, but not holy
Idol worship: forbidden, but not a קרבן
Ordinary, non-holy food

phrases.english: Since it teaches 'like pig meat',
'like idol worship',
for that reason it teaches 'חולין'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge against רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the redundancy and explains it as a listing that came along with the other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case in a משנה must teach a new law
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חולין' was listed only because the other non-binding vows were being listed

steps.title: רבינא: 'חולין' teaches that no שאלה is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reads all three cases as one list. He says 'חולין' was included to show that none of these vows even need שאלה to a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is what the משנה means: 'And these are permitted: like חולין, like pig meat, like עבודה זרה.' If it had not taught חולין, I would have thought these vows still need שאלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different answer. In his reading, 'חולין' does teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'חולין' in the list, we might think that pig meat and עבודה זרה are not real vows, but still need a חכם to release them, just to be safe. Since 'חולין' clearly needs nothing at all, putting it in the same list shows that all of them are fully permitted with no שאלה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say: a rereading of the משנה
Asking a חכם to release a vow
I would have thought

phrases.english: רבינא said:
This is what it teaches: 'And these are permitted:'
'like חולין', 'like pig meat', 'like idol worship'.
And if it had not taught חולין,
I would have said it requires a request to a חכם.
phrases.notes: He means the vow doesn't really take effect, but you might still think it should be released by a חכם, just to be careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the redundancy challenge, different from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה so that 'חולין' teaches a new law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Vows using pig meat or עבודה זרה might still need שאלה
steps.terutzMaskana: Including 'חולין' shows that all these vows are completely void and need no שאלה

steps.title: The end of the משנה already shows no שאלה is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא. The סיפא about 'like my mother' already shows that the earlier cases need no שאלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could anyone even think that? The end of the משנה teaches that if a man says to his wife, 'You are to me like my mother', we open an opening for him from a different angle. That shows the earlier cases need no שאלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's answer. It says nobody would ever have thought these vows need שאלה, so 'חולין' is not needed to teach that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא singles out the 'like my mother' case as needing release, through a פתח from a different angle. That means the earlier cases in the משנה do not need any release at all. So we already know this without 'חולין'.

keyTerms.term: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְאַסּוֹקֵי עַל דַּעְתָּא הָכִי
keyTerms.meaning: Would anyone even think this way?
The last part of a משנה
We open an opening for him: the חכם finds a basis to release the vow
It can be inferred that

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְאַסּוֹקֵי עַל דַּעְתָּא הָכִי?
phrases.english: But is there anyone who would think this way?
Why, since the last clause teaches:
one who says to his wife, 'You are to me like my mother',
we open an opening for him from a different place,
phrases.notes: The חכם finds some other reason to release him, and doesn't mention that the vow was weak to begin with.

phrases.english: this shows that the first clause does not need a request!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְאַסּוֹקֵי עַל דַּעְתָּא הָכִי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that 'חולין' teaches that no שאלה is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא already implies that the earlier cases need no שאלה, so 'חולין' is not needed to teach that.

steps.title: Conclusion: 'חולין' was mentioned only in passing
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's answer is rejected. The clear explanation is that 'חולין' was mentioned only incidentally.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: 'חולין' was mentioned just in passing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבינא's answer and settles the question. 'חולין' teaches nothing new; it was just listed along with the other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This returns to the first answer from step 3. The משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the 'חולין' case is there only because of the list, not for a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is clear: the גמרא's final decision
It was mentioned in passing, only as a side point

steps.whatToRemember: The 'חולין' case in the משנה follows רבי יהודה and teaches nothing new. It is listed in passing next to pig meat and עבודה זרה. רבינא's idea that it teaches 'no שאלה needed' is rejected, because the סיפא already shows that.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear:
the case of חולין was cited just in passing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא after the challenge in step 5 and goes back to the answer in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'חולין' appears in the משנה only incidentally; it adds no new law.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a נדר only works when it is linked to a דבר הנדור.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that a נדר only works if you compare something to an item forbidden by a נדר. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps assumed that comparing something to pig meat or to עבודה זרה (things the תורה forbids) does not create a נדר. Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these words? (asking for a source)
An item that became forbidden through a vow

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the rule from the earlier steps: a נדר has to be tied to something forbidden by a vow, not by the תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how to read the משנה, the גמרא now looks for the source of the basic rule behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a נדר must be linked to a דבר הנדור.

steps.title: The source: a vow must be linked to a vowed item
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'איש כי ידר נדר לה׳' teaches that a person must make his vow by comparing to a דבר הנדור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'When a man vows a vow to ה׳.' This means a vow does not work until he vows using something that is itself forbidden by a vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The word 'נדר' teaches that the item you compare to must itself be a 'vowed' item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ידר נדר', 'vows a vow.' The גמרא reads this as: the prohibition you are borrowing must come from a נדר. So comparing to pig meat, which the תורה forbids, does not create a נדר.

keyTerms.meaning: He vows a vow

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״אִישׁ כִּי יִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַה׳״ —
phrases.english: The verse states: "When a man vows a vow to the Lord"
until he vows with an item that is forbidden by a vow.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'ידר נדר' teach that the vow must be linked to a דבר הנדור.

steps.title: But the same פסוק also mentions a forbidden item
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק goes on to say 'לאסור אסר', which sounds like comparing to a דבר האסור should work too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then a vow linked to an item forbidden by the תורה should also work, because it is written 'to bind his soul with a bond (אסר).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The next words of the same פסוק seem to include items forbidden by the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אסר' sounds like 'אסור', forbidden. That suggests that linking a vow to anything forbidden, even by the תורה, should create a נדר. That would go against what the גמרא just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
An item forbidden by the תורה itself
To bind with a bond (a phrase in the פסוק about vows)

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ בְּדָבָר הָאָסוּר נָמֵי,
phrases.english: If so, even with an item forbidden by the Torah, it should also work,
for it is written: "To bind his soul with a bond"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ בְּדָבָר הָאָסוּר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only a דבר הנדור works.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'לאסור אסר' in the same פסוק seems to include a דבר האסור.

steps.title: That phrase is needed for a different teaching
steps.stepSummary: 'לאסור אסר' is used for a ברייתא's teaching and cannot be used to include a דבר האסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'to bind with a bond' are needed for what a ברייתא teaches: 'What is the bond mentioned in the תורה...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase 'לאסור אסר' is already used for another teaching. So it does not prove that a דבר האסור works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא quoted earlier (on 12a) learns from 'לאסור אסר' what kind of 'bond' the תורה means. Linking to something already forbidden by an earlier vow works, but linking to something the תורה forbids does not. Since the phrase is used up for that teaching, it cannot include a דבר האסור, so the rule from step 8 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
As a ברייתא teaches
A 'bond', meaning a prohibition a person takes on himself

steps.whatToRemember: A נדר only works when the speaker compares to something forbidden by a נדר, like a קרבן. Comparing to something the תורה forbids does not create a נדר.

phrases.english: "To bind with a bond" is needed for that which is taught in a baraita:
What is the bond mentioned in the Torah, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points to the rest of the ברייתא brought earlier on 12a.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase is already used for another teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לאסור אסר' would include even a דבר האסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase is used for the ברייתא's teaching, so only a דבר הנדור works.

steps.title: A ברייתא contradicts the משנה about 'like my mother'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה treats 'you are like my mother' as needing a חכם, but a ברייתא says such words mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who says to his wife 'You are like my mother...' And a contradiction is raised: 'You are to me like the flesh of my mother, like the flesh of my sister, like ערלה, or like כלאי הכרם — he has said nothing!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of 'like my mother' and points out that a ברייתא seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that this man needs to go to a חכם to undo his words. But the ברייתא says 'he has said nothing,' which sounds like he does not even need a חכם. Both cases compare to things the תורה forbids, so why the difference?

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction
Fruit of a tree in its first three years
Forbidden mixed plantings in a vineyard
He has said nothing

steps.confusionAlert: Both sources agree that the vow does not truly take effect. The only question is whether he still has to go to a חכם.

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשְׁתּוֹ הֲרֵי אַתְּ כְּאִימָּא כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: One who says to his wife: You are like my mother, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which says a חכם must be involved to undo his words.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
You are to me like the flesh of my mother,
like the flesh of my sister, like orla, or like diverse kinds in a vineyard —
he has said nothing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה and raises a contradiction against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that 'like my mother' needs a חכם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says such a statement is meaningless, so no חכם should be needed.

steps.title: אביי: nothing by the תורה, but a חכם by the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא means it has no power by תורה law, while the משנה requires a חכם by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'He has said nothing' by תורה law, but he needs to ask a חכם by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by explaining that the two sources talk about two different levels of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'he said nothing' means the vow does not take effect מדאורייתא. The משנה adds that the רבנן still require him to go to a חכם. So both are true at the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: By תורה law
By rabbinic law
Asking a חכם to undo a vow

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He has said nothing by Torah law,
but he needs a request to a sage by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two levels of law (תורה law versus rabbinic law)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He said nothing' means no חכם is needed at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the vow has no force מדאורייתא, yet the רבנן still require שאלה.

steps.title: רבא: scholars versus unlearned people
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא is about תלמידי חכמים and the משנה is about an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This one (the ברייתא) is about תלמידי חכמים; that one (the משנה) is about an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. The two sources are talking about two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תלמיד חכם knows such words mean nothing, so he needs no חכם. An עם הארץ might come to take vows lightly, so the רבנן require him to go to a חכם. אביי splits by level of law; רבא splits by the person speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah scholars
An unlearned person

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction about 'like my mother' has two answers: אביי (no force by תורה law, but שאלה by rabbinic law) and רבא (no שאלה for scholars, שאלה for an עם הארץ).

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is referring to Torah scholars,
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is the ברייתא that says 'he said nothing.'

phrases.english: that is referring to an ignoramus.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא בְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, הָא בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same contradiction that אביי answered in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into different cases (different kinds of people)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה are about the same person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about scholars, who need no שאלה; the משנה is about an עם הארץ, who does.

steps.title: Support for רבא from a vow made by the Torah
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a vow 'by the תורה' means nothing. רבי יוחנן adds that the person still needs a חכם, and רב נחמן adds that a תלמיד חכם does not. This matches רבא's split between scholars and ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: someone who makes a vow by the Torah has not said anything. And רבי יוחנן said: he still needs to ask a חכם to release him. And רב נחמן said: a תלמיד חכם does not need to ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and two אמוראים to show that רבא's answer (scholar vs. עם הארץ) matches an idea already found elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a vow 'by the תורה' does not work at all. Still, רבי יוחנן says the person must go to a חכם, and רב נחמן limits that to someone who is not a תלמיד חכם. This is exactly רבא's pattern: an empty vow needs a חכם only for an עם הארץ, who might otherwise take vows lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a vow by comparing something to the Torah (a ספר תורה)
He has not said anything; the vow does not take effect
Asking a sage to release a vow
A Torah scholar

steps.whatToRemember: A vow that does not really take effect still needs a חכם for an ordinary person, so he will not treat vows lightly. A תלמיד חכם does not need one. This is רבא's approach, and it is supported by רבי יוחנן together with רב נחמן.
steps.confusionAlert: Usually 'וְהָתַנְיָא' starts a question against what was just said. Here it is the opposite: it brings support for רבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבא's distinction between scholars and ordinary people is not a one-time answer. It is a known rule that applies to other empty vows too.

phrases.english: And it was taught: one who vows by the Torah
phrases.notes: He means he linked his vow to a ספר תורה, which is holy, but its holiness does not come from a vow, so it is not a דבר הנדור.

phrases.english: has not said anything.
And רבי יוחנן said:
But he needs to ask a sage.
And רב נחמן said:
And a Torah scholar does not need to ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: הַנּוֹדֵר בַּתּוֹרָה — לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רבא's answer in step 13
steps.raayaObject: רבא's distinction: a vow that does not take effect still needs a חכם for an עם הארץ but not for a תלמיד חכם
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about vowing by the Torah, with comments from רבי יוחנן (a חכם is still needed) and רב נחמן (a תלמיד חכם does not need one)
